criteria.note: warp_api_runner.py ships at plugin/templates/scripts/runners/api/, reads a JSON journey (base_url + steps of method/path/headers/body + expect), and drives HTTP via stdlib urllib.request.urlopen (verified real: tamper showed observed 'got 200', no-server showed 'Connection refused'). All six expect kinds are genuinely evaluated in assert_expect: status, max_seconds, json_keys, json_equals, json_path_present, json_path_equals. No vacuous pass path - a missing top-level key or unresolved path appends a named failure (not silently ignored); json_keys/json_equals fail if body is not a dict; non-JSON body with a JSON assertion fails. run() stops at the first failing step (break) and records step label (index:METHOD path) + every failed assertion; exits 0 all-pass else 1.

Ran test_api_runner.sh: stands up the stdlib mock server, pass.journey.json exits 0, fail.journey.json exits 1 (failure caught), script exits 0. Independently tampered a copy of pass.journey.json three ways against the live mock: wrong status (expect 500 vs 200), wrong json_equals value, and an absent json_path asserted present - each exited 1 with the specific assertion named; the runner passed no false assertion. A transport error (no server) is a named step failure (exit 1). Confirmed a real 4xx is assertable-as-pass: expecting 404 on a 404 route passes (exit 0), proving HTTPError responses are returned and asserted, not stubbed.

Ran python3 scripts/selftest.py -> 161 passed, 0 failed. The api-runner block imports the runner + mock server, exercises every expect kind for BOTH true and false outcomes (status, json_keys, json_equals, json_path_present, json_path_equals, max_seconds), the JSON-path resolver true+false, non-JSON body, and run() fail-closed on missing base_url; then starts MS.serve(0) on an ephemeral port in a daemon thread and drives the runner over the shipped pass fixture (passed=True) and fail fixture (passed=False, failure named). In-process, no external dependency; verify.sh gate stays GREEN.

Case-insensitive grep for company/product names (bcengi, dejitech, travelpass, workpass, agentpass, coreconnect, onesim, mvne, dmitry, tripdesk, daybook, stripe, hubspot, affiliate-network, ava) over runner+fixtures+mock_server+wrapper+README = clean. .warp/capabilities.yaml and plugin/templates/.warp/capabilities.yaml are byte-identical (sha256 03a3eead9417eac0...). http_api_runner is marked status: reference with an honest note that the warp repo has no HTTP surface and does not run it. verify.sh docs/genericity/secret/lint/template-sync gates all pass.

findings.text: A step with no expect block passes on transport success alone (assert_expect returns [] for an empty expect). This is documented behavior ('all present keys must hold') and not a rubber-stamp - it requires deliberately omitting the expect block - but an adopting repo should include an expect on every step it wants proven.

proof/WARP-0301/ is git-untracked at HEAD (working artifact); the runner, selftest block, and both capabilities.yaml files ARE committed and clean at fa1be40. Recomputed proof_digest via .warp/policy_check.py.proof_digest(manifest) = sha256:c7ab3c213deed906, matching the expected value.

summary: All four ACs confirmed. The runner genuinely drives HTTP via stdlib urllib and asserts all six expect kinds with no vacuous-pass path; false assertions (wrong status, wrong value, absent path) and transport errors all fail with the offending step and assertion named. test_api_runner.sh passes, selftest is 161/0 with the api-runner block exercising every expect kind true and false against an in-process ephemeral-port server, the artifact is generic (zero company/product names), capabilities.yaml is byte-identical across template and instance and honestly marked status: reference, verify.sh is GATE GREEN at fa1be40, no em/en/double-hyphen in added files, and proof_digest recomputes to sha256:c7ab3c213deed906. No blocking findings; verdict pass.
